_about: Every table in Supabase's public schema, and what the daily private backup (backup-sensitive-data.yml -> scripts/backup-tables.py) does with it. The script reads the live table list on every run and fails if a table isn't named here, so a new table can't go unbacked-up silently (this happened twice: 20 tables in 2026-09, then 16 more by 2026-09-30). 'tables' are backed up, each as database/<table>.json, fetched 1000 rows at a time in the order given (the primary key, so pages don't overlap). 'public_elsewhere' are backed up publicly by backup-cms-content.yml. 'excluded' are left out on purpose, each with its reason.

excluded.th_uptime_checks: Uptime monitoring telemetry: no PII, grows without bound, regenerated by the checker.
excluded.cron_alerts: Cron watchdog telemetry: no PII, regenerated as jobs run.
excluded.cron_tracked_http_requests: Cron watchdog telemetry: no PII, regenerated as jobs run.
excluded.cron_watchdog_state: Cron watchdog's own working state: rebuilt on its next run.
excluded.internal_mfa_gate_log: Two-factor gate telemetry (what log mode would have blocked): reviewed live, not restored.
excluded.internal_mfa_recovery_codes: Hashes of one-time sign-in codes. A restored copy would bring back codes already used or replaced, and copies of sign-in secrets shouldn't multiply; after a restore, people generate new codes.
